Read via `tail -N`, not by loading the whole file -- it's meant to grow indefinitely and stay cheap to check.

session_label: compression experiment Encoder session -- wrap-up
summary: Acted as Encoder for the compression round-trip experiment. Completed 49 scored rounds (of 51 logged (msg,budget) pairs; c001 unscored at 0.3/0.15 due to contamination) across 15 messages x 4 budget levels [0.7,0.5,0.3,0.15]. Found and helped fix TWO real Decoder contamination bugs mid-experiment: (1) a single long-lived Decoder session retaining cross-round memory when decoding multiple budgets of the same message -- fixed by partitioning Decoders one-per-budget-level (baked into DECODER_ROLE.md); (2) even partitioned Decoders got contaminated by broadly reading the shared log.jsonl at session setup (exposed to other messages' compressed_text/reconstructions) -- fixed via a grep-only-your-own-tag discipline. Mean semantic_cosine by budget: 0.7=0.940, 0.5=0.939, 0.3=0.894, 0.15=0.810 (clean degradation curve). Key findings: named-entity/technical/math-formula anchor terms (Rosetta Stone, osmosis, train-speed equations) let world knowledge reconstruct near-full fidelity even at extreme compression; dialogue-with-no-narration genre catastrophically collapses below a viability floor (lowest score in dataset, 0.336, at 7-word compression of pure dialogue); argument/philosophical genre is structurally robust but reliably invents illustrative examples not in the original; customer-service and warning genres are most compression-tolerant due to template-constrained registers; embedding-based scoring penalizes register drift (added formality/elaboration) even when all facts are preserved. Also found one pre-existing math inconsistency in corpus message c015 unrelated to compression.
note: analyze.py had a stale tfidf_cosine reference from before a prior session renamed score.py's metric to semantic_cosine -- fixed in this session (2 lines + docstring). Full round-by-round data with encoding_notes/decoder_notes is in log.jsonl, ready for LEARNED_ENCODING_SPEC.md writeup per PROTOCOL.md.
